reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: none of the quoted provisions restrains Customer's own business, products it may buy, or technology it may independently develop.

p0007 (Field of Use) and p0027 are license-grant scope limits on how Licensee may use/distribute Licensor's Licensed Technology, not covenants barring Licensee from operating competing lines or building its own platform; treating them as license-scope rather than non-compete is a defensible reading of the rule's summary ('restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build').

p0125 is a non-solicitation of Licensor employees (a different playbook topic, and its 3-year post-term tail should be picked up by the non-solicit rule if one exists), and p0134 is a consent/termination right on change of control, correctly routed to the assignment/CoC rule rather than NONCOMPETE.

No redline or counterparty comment is expected for a compliant finding; the rendered paragraphs are unchanged and the deterministic check ('no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains') passes, so the finding is properly retained as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue.

Minor caveat only: the detection guidance references 'field-of-use ... restrictions binding Customer', so if the business wants broader use rights, that should be raised under license-scope rather than as a non-compete deviation; this does not undermine the compliant conclusion.
